title: Trium-XBT target description
description: Declarative description of a ternary hardware target. Validated by this schema, then compiled to C++ by tools/gen_targets.py. Adding a machine means adding a YAML file -- not editing the driver.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file targets.

name.description: Canonical target name, e.g. "riscv64-xbt". Unique across all files.

aliases.description: Alternative spellings accepted on the command line.

family.description: Broad class, used by the backend registry to select a code generator.

datapath.description: The ternary datapath: what one instruction can do.

max_immediate_trits.description: Trits materialisable by a single instruction.

storage.description: How the target stores ternary data.

zero_hardwired.description: Register 0 reads as zero, as in RISC-V.

native_ops.description: Core-profile operation names the target implements in hardware. An empty set means 'assume everything'; anything absent from a non-empty set must be lowered to software or refused.

memory.description: Memory hierarchy. Drives the memory model of docs/TENSOR_MEMORY_MATHEMATICS.md Part III: Track A (implicit movement) vs Track B (explicit movement).

explicit_movement.description: True if the compiler must issue data movement itself (Track B accelerators). False for caches managed by hardware (Track A).

costs.description: Instruction latencies in cycles, keyed by core-profile op name. Drives the instruction selector's cost model. Ops absent from this map get the default_cost.

default_cost.description: Latency for ops not listed in `costs`.

simulator.description: Track B: how to run this target when no silicon exists. `null` means real hardware is available.
